summary.title: Seedance 2.0: Advancing Video Generation for World Complexity

details: Video generation has been limited to short clips with weak controllability; production workflows need robust, natively controllable audio-video synthesis driven by mixed reference material.
Existing models cover only a narrow slice of multimodal reference/editing tasks, forcing users to discover capability boundaries by trial and error.

Seedance 2.0: a native multi-modal audio-video generation model with a single unified architecture that jointly generates video and audio conditioned on any combination of text, image, video, and audio inputs.

Provides an integrated suite of reference and editing operations (subject/motion/style/visual-effects reference, clip and audio editing, forward/backward video continuation) that can be composed within one model, plus binaural multi-track audio synchronized to visuals.

Accompanying contribution: SeedVideoBench 2.0, an evaluation framework adding explicit multimodal task-following/consistency metrics and narrative-quality metrics, split into objective (automated) and subjective (blind expert) tracks.
Outputs 4-15 s audio-video at native 480p or 720p; a 'Fast' accelerated variant for low-latency use.
Open-platform reference inputs: up to 3 video clips, 9 images, 3 audio clips.
Released in China Feb 2026 on Doubao, Jimeng, Volcano Engine (model id doubao-seedance-2-0-260128); no architecture, data, or training details disclosed.
Three tasks: text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video (including editing and extension).

T2V/I2V scored on six dimensions (motion quality, video prompt following, aesthetics or source-image preservation, audio quality, audio-visual sync, audio prompt following) with ~30 fine-grained video categories and 17 audio categories.
R2V scored on multimodal task following and prompt following (1-3 scale) plus editing consistency, reference alignment, motion quality (1-5 scale); also a 22-way multimodal input/task support matrix.
Multimodal tasks grouped into reference, editing, extension, and combination (e.g., swapping a video subject with a reference image).
MOS-style 1-5 expert ratings by media-industry evaluators (advertising, game production), with blind review for subjective dimensions.
Derived rates reported: usability (acceptable), satisfaction (score >=4), delight (score =5).
Separate realism study where evaluators tried to distinguish Seedance 2.0 outputs from real footage, feeding back into aesthetic tuning.
Independent external check via Arena (formerly LMArena) crowd pairwise voting / Elo.
Commercial competitors: Kling 3.0 / Kling 3 Omni / Kling 2.6 / Kling O1, Sora 2 Pro, Veo 3.1, Wan 2.6, Vidu Q2 Pro.

key_findings.finding: Seedance 2.0 ranks first on every evaluated dimension of all three generation tasks in SeedVideoBench 2.0.
key_findings.evidence: In T2V it is the only model above 3.4 on all six dimensions, reaching 3.75 on both motion quality and audio-visual sync (>=0.65 above the runner-up); in I2V it scores 3.31-3.70 while no competitor exceeds 3.18; in R2V it leads all five dimensions (2.50/2.52 on the 1-3 scales; 3.54/3.03/3.24 on the 1-5 scales).

key_findings.finding: The largest advantage over competing commercial models is in audio generation and audio-visual alignment, where rival models are largely unusable.
key_findings.evidence: T2V audio-quality satisfaction is 62.05% versus below 10% for all competitors, and audio-visual sync satisfaction 68.30% versus a competitor high of 25.45%; in I2V audio quality Seedance 2.0 reaches 97.42% usability/57.08% satisfaction while Kling 2.6 and Wan 2.6 fall below 28% usability; only Seedance 2.0 produces any delight-rated (score 5) audio-quality outputs (6.70%).

key_findings.finding: Human preference at scale confirms the internal benchmark gains, with top rank achieved despite lower output resolution.
key_findings.evidence: Dreamina Seedance 2.0 720p ranks #1 on both Arena T2V and I2V leaderboards with Elo 1450 (+/-15) and 1449 (+/-11), leading veo-3.1-audio-1080p by 79 points on T2V and grok-imagine-video-720p by 29 points on I2V, with rank spread 1-1.

key_findings.finding: Motion quality and physical plausibility improved most over the previous in-house generation.
key_findings.evidence: Average T2V gain over Seedance 1.5 is 0.86 points with motion quality up 1.36; motion-quality usability reaches 97.55%; fine-grained categories previously weak improved by over 1.5 points each (physical feedback 1.69, natural phenomena 2.00, intense sports motion 2.00 in Seedance 1.5), and Seedance 2.0 ranks first on 29 of 30 motion categories.
